notes.title: Smalland Update: Guilds, Stables, Vertical Expansion & More!
notes.content:
Greetings Smallfolk! 

We’ve got a major patch going live today that brings a ton of exciting new features and improvements to Smalland: Survive the Wilds. Whether you’re building your dream encampment, exploring the furthest reaches of the Overlands, or bonding with your trusty companion, this update has something for everyone. 

Here’s what’s new: 

[h2]🛡️ Guilds Are Here! [/h2]

You can now form guilds with other players and take your co-op experience to the next level. Guilds are server-centric, saved with the game world.  
[list]
[*] Introducing server-wide player guilds and shared encampments. 
[*] Members can share a Tree Encampment that stays active on the server as long as one guildmate is online. 
[*] Encampment interaction—building, customizing, and reviving—is based on your role. 
[*] A brand new revive consumable lets guild members bring each other back mid-adventure! 
[/list]
[h2]🐾 Stables & Companion Summoning [/h2]
Companions just got a big upgrade! 
[list]
[*] Companions can now be housed in three different types of stables, depending on their size. 
[*] When at your encampment, you can summon companions for free—or use a Summoning Pebble to bring them into the Overlands. 
[*] Left a companion behind? No worries—the new Homecoming Totem lets you call them back to your encampment. 
[/list]
[h2]🌲 New Northern Encampments & a New Creature [/h2]
Venture north and you’ll find: 
[list]
[*] Two new Tree Encampments that connect to the existing network. Talk to Bonniedel to find and activate them. 
[*] A brand new task featuring the mysterious Roufus-Bellied Tit—a never-before-seen creature in Smalland.  
[/list]
[h2]🛠️ Quality of Life, Visuals & More [/h2]
[list]
[*] Extended companion commands for better control and utility. 
[*] Decorative mushrooms for all your cottagecore roofing needs. 
[*] Fixed journal entries for Bonniedel and Granger 
[*] Improved rock materials and world visuals. 
[*] Added an in-game "Give Feedback" option—help shape the future of Smalland! 
[*] Fixed missing toy soldiers from the beach. 
[*] Added Rufous Mask Helmet 
[*] To prevent griefing, it’s prohibited to release Companions in another player’s Tree Encampment 
[*] Ranged weapon rebalancing 
[*] Added social menu 
[*] Fixed an issue where >100 creature level would revert when loading the game 
[*] Plus, a wide range of bug fixes and polish. 
[/list]
As always, thank you for surviving the wilds with us. Your feedback continues to shape each update—so don’t hesitate to try out the new in-game feedback tool and let us know what you think! 
 
 — The Smalland Team

notes.title: 2025 Content Roadmap Reveal – What’s Coming to Smalland!
notes.content:
Survival in Smalland is about to get even bigger. 

We’re thrilled to reveal a sneak peek at what’s coming in 2025 — packed with brand-new features, long-requested additions, and quality-of-life improvements that will make your adventures even more immersive, strategic, and fun. 

Whether you’re a seasoned player or a newcomer, there’s never been a better time to explore the world of Smalland. 

[h2]🆕 New Features Coming in 2025[/h2]

Here’s a look at some of the major additions arriving this year: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/24470172f6bfa683df2a8e0f1ed406d2a7bd4b95.jpg[/img]

🪶 Creature Stables – Safely store and manage your loyal creature companions. 

🛡️ Creature Equipment – Outfit your mounts with gear to give them new abilities or bonuses. 

🗣️ Creature Commands – Issue direct commands to your companions for better tactical control during exploration or combat. 

🛡️ Guilds – Team up with fellow players and form your own Guilds to share an encampent, tackle challenges together, and unlock new features. 

🧍 Expanded Customization – We're expanding personalization options so you can better express your character's style. (More details coming soon!) 

🕳️ Caverns & Crystals – New subterranean areas to explore, filled with unique resources, glowing crystals, and fresh environmental storytelling. 

[h2]🌲 Other Additions [/h2]

🌿 Two New Encampment Trees – You will be able to build your base in two locations in the northen area of the map. 

[h2]🔁 Crossplay is Coming! [/h2]

One of the most anticipated features is finally on its way: Crossplay support is coming later in 2025! 
Soon, you’ll be able to team up with friends no matter what platform they play on — and we’ll have more details to share on this soon. 

[b][i]This is just the beginning. [/i][/b]
We’re committed to building a rich, thriving world in Smalland — and everything here is only a piece of what’s in store. The team is actively working behind the scenes to bring even more enhancements, surprises, and community-driven improvements throughout the year. 

We can’t wait to share more. Stay tuned, and thank you for being part of this incredible journey!

notes.title: Smalland: Survive the Beta!
notes.content:
[h2]Hey everyone!
[/h2]
In order to improve our game as much as possible, we've decided to make a major update to Smalland's balancing world. 

And to achieve the best possible changes, we'd like to get you involved and hear your feedback! That's why we're officially announcing the immediate availability of the beta test branch on Steam! 

[b]How do I get in?
[/b]
It's very simple:
1) Go to your Steam library
2) Go to the game properties
3) In the “Beta” tab
4) In “Beta test programs"
5) Select ”public_test"
6) Close the window, an update is launched and you're ready to play!

notes.title: Patch Notes #13: The Taming Update
notes.content:
Greetings Smallfolk! 

It's time to show you what features we're giving you and your creatures, all a part of our Taming Update! We've got some highly requested features in here that we've been working on for a while!

[previewyoutube=wTouRQj_pFM;full][/previewyoutube]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/4393829368859bd56963951221af34dfc6fed80e.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/aa40a0524af97048462503fc8ff91e4db003c79f.gif[/img]

Traps are exactly what they sound like - craft-able mechanisms unlocked from the get-go. The baits for these will need to be unlocked at familiar NPCs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/b7c549001b10204ae865bb3ee671b5fb7c13f47a.png[/img]

There are four tiers of trap: Basic, Improved, Advanced and Superior. Each higher tier offers an increased chance at being able to capture your soon-to-be pal. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/c77fff2ab80d70a5d698bfbdef7f4d0616d3e480.png[/img]

But how does one tame, you ask? It's simple. Place your trap down and creatures will be attracted to the bait within. They will then trigger the trap mechanism, where you will then wait a moment to see if your trap has been successful!

Alternatively, you can aggro a select creature, engaging them in combat, weakening them and then placing the trap for improved capture chance!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/56e163f24a743a4709affb05e6ed4e80b885fbc9.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/e55d5b09a827e311bf7b13a5d704c759fcd320ba.gif[/img]

With this new system, we've expanded the taming pool, so nearly every creature in Smalland: Survive the Wilds are now tamable!

This includes Jumping Spiders, Cockroaches, Stinkbugs and many more, with now 38 tames in total.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/e296752e98a4c3a1b280e7286cc67077054844b5.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/997dba0f1649c22d2d325319b5cd597f68eb8da7.gif[/img]

We have also expanded your party size, so you can now tame and have more than one creature following you at a time!

There is now a set party budget (total of 100) that you can use to have numerous creatures active at once. Each creature's value will be different based on level and species. 

So you can combine lots of low budget creatures, such as Ants and Ladybugs, or a couple of high budget creatures like Geckos and Scorpions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/d254bf057726af7d28819bbb29b81a2f0c74ace5.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/1639a1d04ef561fd60ce3c9c0a2ecc3252404ed2.png[/img]

With this update also comes traits! There are over 15 different traits that will generate when you tame your creature. These come in four tiers: Common, Uncommon, Rare and Legendary. These range from being slightly more durable to even having a healing aura.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/4f08e16bab4c52ffdf5aa14d96f0f2dd6c856faf.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/3e4a7161a200f02d5d394d89a81c1817dacaadec.gif[/img]

Can you pet the bugs? Yes. You can pet the bugs.
This increases bond with your companion, and higher bond means they can take more and deal more damage, through the power of love and friendship of course.

If the bond hits zero, your creature may release themselves out of neglect...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/601f875354bb02cdb659467c8b1df0b7464c8002.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/83c4c90408e9651e99b7f842d7a787ae62cbc69b.gif[/img]

Additionally, killed creatures don't die. That makes sense, give me a moment. 
When a tamed creature's health hits zero, they will be incapacitated until someone or something either finishes them off, or until you use a revive incense to bring them back to life, craftable at the work bench.

Remember, if the incapacitated creature takes too much damage, it will die - so make sure to rev your pet before they perish!

This also has a toggle in the world menu, so that incapacitated creatures can't be killed!

Known issues:[b]Mounting for the jumping spider has been temporarily disabled while we work on a fix. [/b]

Also, to celebare Smalland's including in Steam's Survival Craft Festival, we've partnered with the excellent folks at Fireshine and Pugstorm for a Smalland and Core Keeper bundle! This will be live when this post is 2 hours old!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/a21a706b54c25d6899363f8d4b9c95bc994c3e63.png[/img]

That's all for now Smallfolk - don't miss out on upcoming teases!

notes.title: Coming Soon, Events & Factions
notes.content:
Greetings Smallfolk! 

On February 15th with content update #4, we will be introducing events and factions, adding liveliness to the overworld! This system comes with some unique rewards, gameplay situations and replayability!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/dc8c014ab56d4ae5ab2bcfb5da0402e6f1877645.png[/img]

First up, the events themselves.

This is the first iteration of the event system that covers the groundwork of things to come

On debut of this system, there will be several possible combat scenarios that will spawn across the overworld, so make sure you're well equipped!

These events will appear once every 15-20 minutes and 'trigger' once you are near.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/c96b07ed674e015eae847ff2052d787ecdacb00d.png[/img]

Upon successfully completing an event, you will be awarded 'contribution points', these points, can be, well, given towards any of the current four factions; Ants, Spiders, Beasts and Bees! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/38a4c9eac9c7ae782e4dfc864e465905a8a65969.png[/img]

Each faction can also be traded with, offering tradeable armor sets and cosmetic building parts.

Once you contribute 1000 points to a faction, you can align with them to unlock a unique perk, The greater your contribution and the more store tiers that you cap out, the greater the benefit of the affiliation. These perks have various effects that help make characters more powerful in combat, better at surviving, better at taming, or better at resource gathering.  

You can find each faction representative at Mirmek, Lisanda, Skadi and Drustana.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/c08c18f71496d082fbbba6328d4c28a2a9a9beae.png[/img]

notes.title: New Crafting and Enhancement Systems Explained
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/18c27bf8f177f23b97d50b875770e706dbe07765.jpg[/img]

One of the biggest under-the-hood improvements made to Smalland: Survive the Wilds in the Amber Valleys update is an overhaul of the crafting system. Here's what has changed and how it works...

[b]Item Quality[/b]
At the point of crafting a weapon or armour, your intelligence stat is taken into account and may affect the quality of the item. Intelligence doesn't translate directly to a specific quality tier being crafted, instead the more points you have in intelligence, the greater the chance of crafting higher quality items. 

[b]Item Enhancement[/b]
At the workbench, there is now a new tab to Enhance weapons and armour. For a cost, any weapon or armour piece can effectively be upgraded to be as good as the next tier/item type in progression. 

This means that if you prefer to keep an early game sword to match your play style, instead of swapping to a more recently added weapon with better stats, you can now enhance that sword so it remains useful even in late game encounters!

Please note: there is a maximum enhancement tier which is capped at the latest items in the game, so whilst most items can be enhanced up to 3 times, there can be a limit if the item is already late game gear.

[b]Dismantling and recovering resources[/b]
Crafted items can now be dismantled to recover some of their component costs. Dismantling does not provide a full refund for any items it is applied to. The amount of resources that you receive for dismantling may be lower if the item has low durability. 

[b]Respec Attributes[/b]
Player attributes can now be reset at Herne for a cost. To restore all of your invested stat points, simply visit Herne at his camp by the Burrows entrance and select the dialogue option which asks to "refocus my training".

notes.title: Fire Away! Bombs, Handcannons and Anti-Air Turrets!
notes.content:
Lock and load, Smallfolk, steady your hand and flex your trigger finger because you're packing heat now!

[h3]Content Update3: The Amber Valleys, comes 16/10[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/3d78c4ecb7ec088d9e8366815b6a83aa87362fb5.gif[/img]

Introducing the Handcannon. It's a cannon that fits in your hand. Self-explanatory, right? The Handcannon shoots iron ammo, crafted using firesand, a new resource within the Amber Valleys. 

Don't think it's going to mean an easy win in every fight though. While the Handcannon is powerful, it's also closer to an old fashioned musket in function, and takes time to load and prime for each shot. You'll need to be smart in how you use it to get the best effect.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/61b88b7802f3f5fff952364b68a5270099927003.gif[/img]

Another use for firesand is that you can also bundle it up into a nice little grenade - extra lethal against ladybugs!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/f78e42e3ff9efc0c992c1c369c8ee72e75666ba5.gif[/img]

And you're going to need every advantage to take down the new Aetherin turrets. The valley is dotted with these defensive outposts, which will blast away at anything which flies within range - including birds and Smallfolk with wings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/dd5c51df504993255d60757b62e76490287bbd4d.gif[/img]

If you've only just earned your bird, don't worry too much if it gets shot down. One hit isn't lethal, but will cause health loss. Repeatedly trying to fly through Aetherin airspace will risk losing your feathered friend, so if you want to reclaim these lands, you'll need to approach each turret on foot, and defeat the squad of Aetherin that emerges. Doing so will disable that turret permanently.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/3afdf5559b941b269639bcd80e431e2d373bfbd6.gif[/img]

To begin crafting with firesand, you'll need to first meet Granger, a dusty old Smallfolk who now lives as a reclusive beetle rancher in the Amber Valleys.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/38d6f426cde02aa1ac0ca8ac704209734fda80b3.png[/img]

notes.title: Bringing a bit of STING to Smalland!
notes.content:
Life in the Amber Valleys can have a sting in the tail. Literally.

[h3]Content Update 3: The Amber Valleys comes 16/10[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/fae6958846dd657362c7cdba135911cb5d761c32.gif[/img]

 The Scorpion is the ultimate enforcer, tanky, agile and most importantly - brutal! At your size, you don't even need to worry about being poisoned when you have a stinger that size through your chest!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/5c7f346a4732ae737ea64a425c37e7115884ad29.gif[/img]

A tamed Scorpion is the perfect mount for the Amber Valleys. Its speed and agility over the rocky, sandy terrain will help you cover the ground distance in order to shut down those Aetherin turrets, and will also prove helpful in facing the other deadly fauna inhabiting the valleys.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/295a571cb177a073ec4c8182676451dc50eaef9c.gif[/img]

Those rapid snip-snap pincer attacks allow the Scorpion to get the upper claw in combat, and when your foe is where you want them, you can expend a hefty amount of stamina to go for a powerful sting with that powerful tail!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/bba99dba1f6ad762e1cbe8b9ec44f215bc9247c5.gif[/img]

Wait, was that a...Tarantula? Yep. The Overland's spider population just got larger and deadlier, with the addition of this monstrous hairy arachnid. Lurking among the rocks and cliffs, these beasts will test even the hardiest Smallfolk warrior, so watch your step when exploring!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/97f1c03d2802e0d967175d3125d1118bb581fba0.gif[/img]

Of course, there may still be a few surprises in these sun-baked lands. Find out what else is coiled and waiting in store for you on October 16th, when the Amber Valleys update releases!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/78d49793972cea0f7668385871c925c700c2c7e2.png[/img]

notes.title: Prepare to embark into...the Amber Valleys
notes.content:
North of the Forbidden Monuments, where not even the Eagle is foolish enough to patrol, is home to a much more malicious menagerie of chitinous creatures...Smallfolk will need to expand their firepower and gain new wisdom if they wish to survive...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/a0c0ae457d6ec6dcbb8fea3e682ec0d3916e63b0.png[/img]

[h3]Begin the next stage of the Smallfolk story on 16/10/23[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/0336c292de54f2be55963e9f9743075919468cd7.png[/img]

The scorched sands of the Amber Valleys are a marked contrast to the lush greenery you're used to. In corroded caves, across rugged roads, await new threats, fights and frights! So why not take solace at the Oasis, maybe even set up a small outpost and savour your time in the sun, you're a long way away from the Burrows now!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/329beeeef12a55c2591a50ac5d305281baac34db.png[/img]

But you know who isn't far from home? The Aetherin. Those you encountered among the Forbidden Monuments were mere scouts, the Amber Valleys are much closer to their home... 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/1a044361fb98d7c7515c7aa37b420bbd2206abad.png[/img] 

One key thing to learn is that the Aetherin of the Valleys defend their airspace with ruthless efficiency. Using explosive firesand they have constructed turrets to shoot down anyone who tries to encroach on their territory by air.

Don't worry - these turrets may knock your beloved bird out of the sky, but they won't kill them. At least, not immediately. You'll want to set out on foot to lure the Aetherin warriors out of the turrets. Defeat them, and the turret will be permanently deactivated, creating a pocket of safe airspace for your high-flying adventures. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/80f314aaad424735827e06972e905d76564b1e9d.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/76e5e4173e4a2ea64454b2de7d677c2f85a4b6e5.png[/img]

Though, powerful as they are, the Aetherin aren't the dominant threat in this barren land. They worship a new and deadly creature, unique to the Amber Valleys. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/b6dfd6f575c94cbe031b0a0541432636736ed8ba.png[/img]

We have more to come tomorrow, with details on the local wildlife, including creatures unlike anything the Smallfolk have battled before!

notes.title: Smalland: Survive the Wilds 1.0 Release Date Announcement
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=JoboGBGHmj4;full][/previewyoutube]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/f1736547d54a411a0a6cc3f02817b5fbbfce5c7b.png[/img]

A new beginning beckons for the Smallfolk! We’re proud to announce that Smalland: Survive the Wilds will leave Early Access and hit v1.0 on 7th December 2023. 

Does this mean we’ve released all the content updates? 

Not at all. Our third major content update arrives very soon – keep watching for details of that in the next few weeks. As with previous updates, this will add a completely new area to the map, new creatures to battle and tame, more story and NPCs, extra armour, weapons, tools and resources, plus lots of QoL improvements and core system upgrades.  

Another content update of comparable size will coincide with the 1.0 launch. This will bring the initial Smalland: Survive the Wilds story to a close, and form the complete base game that new players will experience as a single seamless experience from 1.0 onwards. 

Is there anything to come after 1.0? 

Yes! We’re also committed to a calendar of updates post-launch, continuing to expand the game with even more new content and improvements to systems and functionality. Details of this post-release roadmap will follow the 1.0 launch. 

And what about…? 

Consoles? Glad you asked. Alongside Smalland: Survive the Wild’s PC 1.0 release, we’re excited to reveal that the game will also launch digitally on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on the same day – 7th December. Both PlayStation and Xbox versions will have the same content as PC at launch. A physical retail release of the console version will follow on 8th December. Cross platform is something we are looking into!

We’re very aware that often the arrival of 1.0 signals the end for an Early Access game, but we really want you – our dedicated earliest players – that for Smalland: Survive the Wilds it really is just the beginning. There are many more stories to tell with the Smallfolk and we’re thrilled you’ve been with us on this journey from the start.

notes.title: A Closer Look At Levelling Up!
notes.content:
The creatures are getting stronger Vanguard, can you say the same for yourself?

With the new experience and attributes system, you can!

Whenever you kill, harvest, or complete a key story moment, you will be rewarded with experience points.
Different creatures and resources will reward different amounts of experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/40efe03a7c9928e955fbcdba3442bd098e719b8d.gif[/img]

In turn, this will give you points that can be spent in four areas; 

[list]
[*] Strength determines how much damage you deal
[*]  Dexterity increases movement speed
[*] Constitution increases base health
[*] Endurance increases base stamina
[/list]

Player characters have a level cap of 100. You will not need to start a new character to take advantage of this. All existing characters will be designated Level 1 when the the Forbidden Monuments update goes live on Thursday. 

More experienced players with more powerful gear and armour will naturally level up faster, so we anticipate all characters will quickly reach the level they would have been at had the levelling system been in place when they were first created.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/3035927cc09d7a890f41f948617ba147eac60175.png[/img]

Though these new levels and attributes aren't just for you! You can level up your tamed creatures to level 10 and increase their stats. 

Creatures will spawn in the wild at different levels, so you might even want to search around using antenna mode to find a creature with a desirable baseline of stats before taming so you can get the tankiest or fastest creature you can!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/093f253b86272cf2fbf75f5d72d3637f9426989e.png[/img]

Rest assured, we will be monitoring and refining this system to give you folks a fulfilling and balanced experience.

Located at the North of the map, the Forbidden Monuments is a hallowed place in Smallfolk lore, filled with towering remnants of Giant civilisation. What bizarre rituals did they perform here? What is the meaning of the strange relics strewn on the ground?

Smallfolk scholars have debated this for centuries - but you'll have no time to ponder the answers if you brave this high level area.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/badec5898ddf26912bacd632cca6208cc1713a20.png[/img]

Ringed by a fence, with an old dead tree in the centre, the Forbidden Monuments offer the most challenging creatures the game has to offer. Stinkbugs will inflict area-of-effect poison attacks, while territorial Blue Tit birds will swoop down and land devastating attacks from above.

And, if the whispers among the Vanguards are true, those may not be your only threats...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/e969cc4d7bc8f77b0047799407cba81b79a371d0.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/4f512b663d6e2ac7b3bc96c98bb1e38ef0f59f80.png[/img]

notes.title: Developer Faq #3
notes.content:
Hey Smallfolk! Here's the next instalment of our dev FAQ Friday, keeping you folks in the loop! This week we're covering some QoL features and options!

[b]Q: Will there be modding support?[/b]
[i]A: Modding support and development is a huge undertaking and all of our mechanics and features are still in development so we can't really work towards that at the moment, however, it is something you folks have expressed a desire for and it is something we really want to consider later down the line.
[/i]

[b]Q: What, if any, are your plans for accessibility improvements? As a visually impaired person, the inventory UI and general environment design could use some more shape and color contrast![/b]
[i]A: It is an ongoing process, we plan on doing a much 'fuller' accessibility pass closer to 1.0 as we know we're missing a few options.
We weren't originally going to add the frequently requested 'arachnophobia mode' - because we asked ourselves 'arachnophobia mode? ''Sure I get that, but what about cockroaches? The mosquitoes? The beetles? They're just as terrifying! Do we need to do all of those as well!?''
But we do, generally, cave to frequently requested features haha.   
[/i]

[b]"Q: Are you planning on adding more seasonal exclusive harvests, creatures and items? 
like pretty pink blossoms in spring, fallen leaves and acorn at fall, Snowdrops flower in the winter?"[/b]
[i]A: Without spoiling any of our upcoming plans, we can say that seasonal events and surprises are absolutely something we are looking to implement. What form these will take, we can't reveal just yet![/i]

[b]Q: "If you guys haven't already, can you make it so more a player can tame more than one bug?
I get too attached to my tames to get rid of them for another."[/b]
[i]A: We love our tames as well, so this is an area where we are definitely keen to introduce more features and interactions, based on player feedback. We can't give details just yet, but rest assured cool things are coming for our critter pals! [/i]

See you next week Smallfolk! We'd love to answer a lot of questions but there's only so much we can reveal! Stay tuned!

notes.content:
Hey Smallfolk! As we continue up to content update #1 it's important to keep you in the loop! We see a lot of questions pop-up here and there, so we're continuing with our weekly dev FAQ!


[b]What are the plans for fast travel?[/b]
[i]Things are coming very soon to help with faster mobility. Short term, we're intending to add very quick ways to get around, although not instantaneous travel. This is an area we'll definitely be looking into further once other priority features are added and we hit a map-size that necessitates fast-travel. [/i]

[b]Dedicated servers when? And I don't mean official servers but being able to rent a server if that makes any sense.. 😂[/b]
[i]This is being worked on and we hope to have news in the coming months, it's a huge endeavor and one that really needs a lot of time and expertise. [/i]

[b]Will there be dedicated servers for pvp?[/b]
[i]"There are plans to introduce dedicated server support at a later date. 
Players will have the option to make them PvP or not. "[/i]

[b]Will we get gear that will allow us to fly instead of glide?[/b]
[i]New armours are planned for most of the content updates leading up to and beyond the full game launch. Some of these will come with new movement abilities. We need to be mindful of player progression and development, once you can fly, what comes next? Faster flying? Even faster flying? Warp-like teleportation? There become fewer options the faster we power-creep.[/i]

[b]"Are you planning to add a feature where you can use resources stored in a container for 
workbenches in the same room? It's a pain constantly gathering and sorting resources from containers"[/b]

notes.title: Dev FAQ Friday #1
notes.content:
Hello Smallfolk! 

Each week, we'll be selecting some of the most frequent questions asked by the community from across every platform to help 'peel back the curtain' and give you some insight into our plans and what we're up to! We'll be aiming for five questions each week across different topics. 

[b]Q: In earlier dev blogs, there were more options for player customization such as hairs with 
multiple colors. Will we see additions like this in the future? 
Will this also come along with an option to hide your helmet, as it seems strange the game starts
 you out with customizing your character only for you to never see your 
face again within a few hours of gameplay.[/b]

[i]A: There are plans to increase the character customisation options both on creation and at the scrying pool. Options to allow customised character features to be visible while wearing armour are being investigated, though no final decisions have been made yet. 

Please, do let us know what type of antenna, hair style, skin-tone and other customisations you'd like to see in future updates..[/i]

[b]Q: What is the dev team's vision for the game? I've seen a few people 
advocate for improvements with PVP in mind but from my time playing and the 
general messaging on social media it doesn't look like it's the primary or even secondary 
focus of the game. Will Smalland set itself apart from other survival games by focusing
 more on PVE and co operation than a PVP experience?[/b]

[i]A: We are definitely planning to accommodate players who want the PVP experience. However, the survival genre already offers many PVP focused titles and the team is keen that Smalland will primarily focus on a PVE experience. For that reason, when we do introduce formal PVP features they will be entirely optional. The core of the project remains targeted at collaborative and PVE based experiences.[/i]

[b]Q: Devs : How do you see the creature companions developing in 
terms of uses and interactions?[/b]

[i]A: We know players love their mounts, so tamed and mountable creatures are something that we want to put focus on throughout the whole of the early access cycle. Plans to make these creatures more functional and interactive are already in the works. We've also received some excellent ideas from player feedback. Please keep letting us know what you'd like mounts to do, and we'll see what's possible! [/i]

[b]Q: what size are smallfolk? like height wise?[/b]

[i]A: Smallfolk are roughly one inch, or two and half centimetres, tall. This isn't an exact science though, as some creative license has been taken with how we represent scale to make gameplay and visuals work together.[/i]

[b]Q: is there any intention to add an auto sort button to inventory or containers?[/b]

[i]This is one of the most common community quality of life requests right now and while we can't confirm how or when we'll be addressing it, please be assured we're currently actively investigating it.[/i]

[/u]

The challenges you face may seem trivial when you're many feet tall... but you'll learn that the danger is relative to your size. You'll need to learn the lay of the land, how to navigate, and how to build your overland home. 

As one of the first of your people to come to the lands above, it's up to you to develop your survival skills to tame the world around you and learn its secrets. The survival of your people depends on it. 

[u]Watch the trailer now![/u]
[previewyoutube=_7eg-4Q-0Rw;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: FAQ Friday #18
notes.content:
Hey Smallfolk!

We're back to dive a little deeper into some of your questions that we've picked up from the community!

[b]How does the season system work?[/b]

Seasons touch the game world in a number of ways. Firstly, the visuals. You can expect bright, sunny days in the summer, and gloomy, grey days in the winter. The landscape will change to reflect, with the leaves turning from fresh greens to the mellow shades of autumn and disappearing entirely in some cases in the winter.

Weather will change depending on the season too, and in gameplay terms, you'll want to prepare your armour setup accordingly when you set out into the world.

Lastly, the wildlife of Smalland will adapt to the seasons, with some creatures being more abundant in one season than another.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/x0wbmQB.gif[/img]

[b]Will there be baby insects and animals and will we also see each stage of insects such as beetles, moths, butterflies etc?[/b]

Insects in Smalland will all appear at the same size, we don't have different stages of growth in the game, though we do currently have baby spiders (approach with caution, mum is never too far away...). There are also some unqiue variations of various insects that will require a little hunting down.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/7b043a064fb182a410c7d9687973e0e47b384ed2.jpg[/img]

[b]Can I play a beta?[/b]

We've been getting asked this a lot lately so a good opportunity to share the process of getting hands-on with any Smalland testing.

We have a group here at Merge Games called the MVP Group, signing up for the group requires agreeing to an NDA, and you can find the details and signup form here [url=https://www.mergegames.com/playtesting]here[/url].

Being a member of the group might see you get offered to join a beta test for a number of different titles, including Smalland. We'll select a segment of testers based on the answers given during signup, some tests will be quite broad and have a large number of keys available, some will be more focused and have fewer keys available.

Currently, builds are watermarked with each user's unique, numerical Steam ID, as a small number of people, unfortunately, chose not to respect the NDA and share footage of a test (which have since been taken down).

Joining the group doesn't guarantee everyone will get hands-on with a particular Smalland test, but that's the place to be if you want to throw your hat into the ring!

As always, thanks for the questions, we'll catch you next time!

Hey Smallfolk!

So as we hijacked a previous FAQ Friday post and kicked off a new series this will be our What We're Working On post #2!

You may have seen some of the latest things we've been tinkering with on social media, so here's so more information about what we've been up to!

[h1]Building[/h1]

The team have been hard at work working on the building system and we've started to get the first of many customisation pieces that you'll be able to unlock and use to make your little house a home.

One of the first is an Owl effigy, a little nod to Discord, and burnt out matches that will become torches!

notes.title: FAQ Friday #17
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

Thanks for Asher on Discord for a bunch of questions that we thought would make a nice FAQ Friday!

Here we go...

[u][b]1. Are there boss fights, dungeons, and hoards?[/b][/u]
There are indeed Boss fights but not dungeons, or what you'd call traditionally dungeons. Everything we do has an element of perspective, so we don't want dungeons to be literally dungeons, instead, you'll be navigating through a dark swamp and across broken dead trees, or trying to figure out a way to get through an overgrown maze while avoiding various hungry predators.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Sxi5KLt.gif[/img]

[u][b]2. Are there caves/holes in the ground?[/b][/u]
Yes and no, the Smallfolk have been living underground for too long, for reasons that will be explained. So your major goal is to make the land safe for your people and out of the ground. However, gameplay-wise, caves etc are usually small pockets of gameplay with risks and rewards that we have. Whether it's inside an abandoned vehicle, a hollow log, or a waste bin, we have the equivalent of caves to explore.

[u][b]3. What is the gameplay like as far as combat mechanics? Are they more akin to dark souls or Skyrim?[/b][/u]
There are attacks and combos, and also weapons that have different effects suited to different creatures and different situations. Some of these must be found and earned, others are crafted. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/X4Cde9S.gif[/img]

[u][b]4. What are the devs thinking as far as pricing for early access/1.0?[/b][/u]
We're not 100% decided on this yet, watch this space.

[u][b]5. Do you level skills up like in Valheim, or is it more or less just crafting items like in Terraria?[/b][/u]
You find items as in Terraria but some of these items can only be earned by aligning with certain factions, or by having access to certain technological advantages, and sometimes a combination of the two. These items may grant you abilities that you can mix and match, specialising in one area or having a hybrid. So the more you explore, craft, and earn via factions, the more you gain access to different skills.

[u][b]6. I heard a while back the map is supposed to be procedurally generated, are they still keeping to that?[/b][/u]
Nope, we've never mentioned that! Everything is being carefully built and crafted by hand.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/1c9a5f01630d1e620b22c58b14c7dc1fe110b7fc.gif[/img]

Thanks for the questions, Asher! We'll be back with more in the next FAQ Friday!

notes.title: FAQ Friday #16
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

I thought I'd hijack this week's FAQ Friday and spend a bit of time on the question of when Smalland is coming out.

It's a question we would love to answer, but we're just not in a position to do so just yet. Smalland has come such a long way over the last year and whilst it's obviously frustrating for some, we don't want to rush out a demo or early access to hit a date, rather we're letting development inform the date and when the time comes to give you some dates we'll be very excited to share that with you.

There's people who have been following Smalland for a few years now, but it's important to note that we acquired Smalland and completely rebooted the game, it's been in full development now for just over a year. Had Smalland not been public prior to the start of our development we would have had a much better timeline from announcement through release, but you can't put the genie back in the bottle! 

So we wanted to tell you a little about what is being worked on by members of the team right now, to try and help give a little context as to why we're not releasing just yet.

One thing that happened this week is that the starting area had a new flora and fauna pass to bring that area closer to our vision of what the release will look like. This isn't just visual, but also from a level design perspective too, things like line of sight and where the scenery leads the player are important to get exactly right. 

For some perspective on how that's come along over the last year, here's a couple of gifs that were shared on Twitter in February 2021.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Q42hqc1.gif[/img]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/ENThi4N.gif[/img]

Here is running around that same general area in the latest build.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/KoijaTg.gif[/img]

As the level design of the game world has developed, so too have other gameplay elements that interact with the world. One of these is something that we have been working on this week, the grappling hook!

The grappling hook has been a point of contention in the team, some love it, some hate it. Some can't use it to save their life, others move through the world like Spider-Man (looking at you Producer Ben!).

[img]https://i.imgur.com/wCsPLbX.gif[/img]

Since earlier stages of development, the verticality of Smalland has really become a part of the experience and as such, we think there's a solid place for the grappling hook and we'll be working on some new implementations for this tool to see what form it will take for the early access. Do you know what will help determine the future of the grappling hook? Player feedback! Stay tuned...

Thanks for your patience, we're a small team making Smalland and we will have more news on the things you really want to know soon. If you like this and want us to delve a bit deeper into specific things that are being worked on behind the scenes, I'll make this a regular thing and pester the team for some fun things to share!

notes.title: FAQ Friday #15
notes.content:
Hey Smallfolk!

[h1]Happy New Year![/h1]

We are so excited for 2022 and what we can share with you, so there are exciting things to come, but we'll still be here to answer those burning questions in the meanwhile!

Without further ado...

[b]Q - Will there be bigger areas on the map that are free of trash and leftovers of humans? Many of the little clips we have seen take place in polluted surroundings.[/b]

A - Yes, truth be told these are easier to create initially so when you see behind the scenes in some of these shots you have some of the more developed areas, whereas the more organic ones take much more time to create. So they look and feel organic, but still have regular gameplay spaces regarding size, height. Initially in the very early days we did lots of experiments and areas either looked right, or felt right, but rarely both, so it meant a lot of level design rules and revisions. But the short answer is yes, lots of overgrown areas.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/371f83791b1ac8b918cc94822b66e91fbabcf7aa.jpg[/img]

[b]Q - Can I only ride my animal friends, or will they protect me like the game horizon zero?[/b]

A - It depends on the creature, some follow and some are mounts when tamed. Mounts have different strengths and weaknesses in different situations. And your allies will sometimes attack when you attack like a loyal steed, or initially retreat but attack if you are attacked, some will attack a creature on the same level of the food chain, while others may run away. Some may also cause trouble and get into fights you might not want to have. We are trying to give the creatures as much personality as possible, but also look and feel like real creatures (which are somewhat expressionless), so this is being portrayed via audio and their behaviour to their surroundings. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/be7f91a5641d21966278b4b8d22906ce8135e005.jpg[/img]

[b]Q - Okay. Sooooo I don't mean to be super technical, but watching your short diary #2 on armour, based on the insect faction you choose to work with, you stated that you are will be able to craft that insects armour, assuming that you will be rewarded with parts to craft blueprints or even the armour its self as rewards.  However, my questions would be based on the armour, is it made from the insects themselves?  And if so is that desecrating their dead to get the items to craft the armour?  I know this seems a little dark but I am just trying to see this from an angle of what others might think as well.  I think the armour sets are really good looking and assuming again that the armour you are showing looks to be like some of the highest tiered armour in the game you will be able to craft toward the end game or much much later.  I would love to hear your feedback.[/b]

A - Great question, hopefully, we can give some of the insight here as this wasn't a quick decision. 
The quick answer is yes, some of the armour is made from the same insect carapace as the species you are aligned with, which in human terms could be somewhat grim. This isn't the case with all creatures, but as an example, Ant armours certainly do use carapaces. This could, as you mentioned, be perceived a little dark but also is in line with one of the major tones of the game; the circle of life. Creatures who are friendly to you may eat one another as predator and prey. And certain creatures will not care about their allies being killed as they put the overall hive first and foremost.

But although we aim to make everything as relatable and realistic as possible, we also want to make sure it's fun and makes sense for gameplay. So in the case of Ants and wearing the Ant armour as a specific example, you have to work with the Ants and you need to earn their trust over time and when worthy, they will trade and gift you some of the elements you need including parts of their fallen for you to create an armour set, which the Smallfolk see as an honour.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/14b49a0465d7164f23a7bff81d352d2871d16f29.jpg[/img]

Thanks for the great questions, as always!

notes.title: Demo & Early Access Announcement
notes.content:
Hey Smallfolk!

We don’t like to share these updates with you, but with community being at the heart of Smalland we wanted to share with you as soon as we made a decision.

[h1]Update on Early Access release & the Demo[/h1]

We have conducted some closed testing sessions recently which have provided so much wonderful feedback. This testing has shown us that there’s more we want to do before we throw open the gates to Smalland. [b]We won't rush anything out.[/b]

There’s two pieces of news to share, one is that the demo will not be coming in October, and the other is that the Early Access release is going to move out of 2021. 

We are [b]committed to bringing a demo out[/b] for Smalland and we’re excited to give players a taste of what awaits them, but the timeline for this is determined by when we’re confident in what we want to show you rather than placing another date in the calendar to work towards. Rest assured we’ll share more as soon as we can.

Both moves are explained by the same motive, which is that we don’t want to put Smalland out until we’re [b]100% confident[/b]. notes.title: FAQ Friday #10
notes.content:
Hey there Smallfolk!

We have some great questions to dive into this week! Let's get into it...

[b]Will you be able to pick a certain map to play on? Because we saw a pool, some gnomes, a forest, and a desert. So can you pick which one to play on?[/b]
Smalland is one big map, no loading between areas. The biomes are quite diverse for different reasons but make up a bigger sandbox game world for you to play in. It takes a while but all the areas you’ve called out are connected, you just have to work out how you’re going to get to each one safely.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/7799efea16344ff122f74737234dbdfcc236b2dc.jpg[/img]

[b]Is there a way you can give a brief summary of how our inventory is going to function?[/b]
We have three categories; Your Quest and Logs which is all the info about what you are doing and why as you create your own narrative. Then there’s everything about your Character, so info such as the current state of your weapons, armour, health, hunger, temperature, dehydration. And then there’s everything Crafting related. 

We have a unified theme but have also tried to distinguish each category at a glance so that each looks and feels intuitive.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/f51454015c8c4b605e03a2f989d17d31eac6abb3.jpg[/img]

[b]With the building of shelters and homes being a large part of the player's role in Smalland, what sort of games have inspired the system you guys want to use for building? E.g in Sims and the forest you can place down and extend walls, but in Ark you place them piece by piece (as far as I'm aware)[/b]
It's a bit of everything really, so different games make their decisions on different gameplay loops, which may look similar but are actually done for very different reasons. For us, the example above is more like Ark, as it's about detail and personalisation, not getting things down quickly. We have camp items that you need for survival that are quick to use, and your overall goal is to build a place for your people in the safety of the trees which takes longer. But you can also build whatever you like wherever is deemed safe. So this all fits within your goals and progression.

One thing to mention is that we have never liked elements that hinder progression with no risk and reward. A great example of this is putting a wall down in the wrong place, it disrupts the flow but also costs resources to remove and re-build. It’s not fun (in our opinion), and as we have a heavy focus on exploration, collecting the resources is where the core gameplay lies, and building is more focused on personalisation with progression elements. So if you destroy something you have built, you get a full refund of resources. 

Initially, we were worried that this may not go down to well with hardcore survival players, but we think is a much better experience….and then Valheim came along and had the same idea, and everyone likes it, which is great, everyone wins :)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/bcd95ff2b179938bdf3c95f22cb8a747e276222f.jpg[/img]

Thanks, everyone, we'll go and find some more of your excellent questions for next time!

notes.title: FAQ Friday #9
notes.content:
Hey there Smallfolk!

Back at it with some more answers to your questions for FAQ Friday #9!

Here we go...

[b]Can you say anything about "tiers of resources"?[/b]
Yeah, that's an in-game term we use, but to explain it… the player has complete freedom of the world, so if you can fight, sneak, glide, fly, jump or however you want to get past the various dangers, you can. So you can get into areas that you are not prepared for. 

Some of these Creatures roaming in certain areas are bigger and deadlier because of their size, others carry venoms that can kill you quickly if you are not prepared. The more deadly the area though, the better the resources, so you could do a lot of grinding in a relatively safe area and have the freedom to build and craft what you like. Or, you could be a little more adventurous as the rewards match the dangers, you find a better quality of resources in these more dangerous/higher tier areas which saves you a lot of time. Entirely up to you, as you have the freedom and your progression is non-linear, it's your choice (and how brave you are feeling).

[b]Will there be multiple different types of weapons such as spears, daggers and maces like Conan or will it just be swords and bows[/b]

We have a range of different weapons that have different classes, and each class has a particular style. For instance, we have Swords which are good all-rounders and Hammers are not ideal against multiple enemies and swarms but are great at delivering a big hit on a creature that outweighs the Smallfolk.

Then there are different types of Bow that suit different purposes, or should I say Creature attacks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/609cda6f2fda3d6e94fff6ad63ff619ae785b3f7.jpg[/img]

[b]Is every creature faction going to have its own armour or are only some going to have armour and others have weapons and other items?[/b]

No, not every creature has its own armour, but also there are Pathfinders that give you valuable knowledge, if you can find them, that also provide Quests and armours. Some Pathfinders allow you to form an alliance with a Creature and then you can learn about its behaviour and how it survives, and how that can benefit the Smallfolk. Some give you armour or armours, some give weapons, some give both.

As always, we love the questions and look forward to reading more of them!

Hey Smallfolk!

We've dived into our 'ask your questions' channel on the [url=https://discord.gg/smalland]Smalland Discord[/url] and pulled out some great questions to answer!

[b]How many players can play at the same time in one world, is the game lobby-oriented, or server-oriented?  Will I be able to build a common town with my entire group of friends?
[/b]
Currently, we are looking at both options and weighing them up. The aim is approximately ten players in a game at once for now. We’re making it as flexible as possible for everyone to play solo, with friends or strangers, to play as a group, or just be in the same world occupied by other people that you can bump into occasionally. Everything has been designed around these principles and we’re aiming for as many players as possible per game.

[b]Are there going to be different animals and insects during the day and the night in the game?[/b]
Yes, Day and Night will affect things, as well as the weather and the seasons, some of these effects will be very minor, others more important to strategy

The weather changes per season as does the temperature which also fluctuates. So the chances of rain, snow are all more likely to be heavier and lower or raise the temperature making it too cold or hot. This is set up to be organic and less scripted, so we create the feeling of a living breathing world, rather than being a repeating and totally reliable process.

notes.title: FAQ Friday #6
notes.content:
Hey Smallfolk!

Back at it with some more answers to community questions! There are lots of new people finding the community so we love the questions and the opportunity to provide some new or expanded information for you!

[u][b]What other sorts of travel options are you guys working on? I saw this and in the other channel some talk about the wings on the armour. I mean, I may be late to the party and missed it, but I'd think the game looks like it should lend itself to some sort of grapple hook or stamina based climbing. Although I figure both of those have likely been answered already.[/b][/u]

Each mount for travel behaves differently and feels different to control with positives and negatives based on its size and its hierarchy within the food chain. These are very powerful and provide a huge amount of freedom in-game, allowing you to venture and explore areas that you may not be prepared for yet. 

Armour also comes with various abilities, mimicking the traits of the Creature or faction it is based on. Some of these are traversal based so there is more planned than just insect wings for gliding. It's up to you to select the right combination of armour and mount which complement one another for the task at hand.

There are also some other elements that can be used for Travel, so watch this space.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/kognLPd.gif[/img]

[u][b]How complex will the crafting/building system be? Is it a big part of the game or is it more like a side thing?[/b][/u]

It’s a big part of the game, building makes your chances of survival stronger. Not only do you need shelter from the elements, but putting time into construction will provide various benefits. It is also your main goal, your role as a Vanguard is to secure a safe place for your people so they can begin to leave the undercity and settle in the Land of the Small where they truly belong.

[u][b]Will all materials in the world be collectable/useable? (i.e. will grass be collectable and actually have a use? or rocks or even, say, metals from the items found around the big world)?[/b][/u]

Yes and no, there is a wide range of natural resources as you’d expect in a survival game. But the trees are huge and you can't just start cutting down trees, they are too thick. Instead, you harvest bark and twigs rather than the main bulk of the tree. Various plants have properties that can be put to good use such as bindings and oils. There are also special items that can be discovered via Quests too which make more unique crafting opportunities. 

[u][b]Will you have to pay to get multiplayer?[/b][/u]

Nope, Smalland is designed to be a PVE game, you can play solo or with friends, or just bump into strangers, joining them or ignoring them in your shared world, its entirely up to you. There is a better chance of survival in larger numbers, and more opportunities for rewards, but how you play is up to you; solo, team, looking for a team, and there is no additional cost.

notes.title: FAQ Friday #5
notes.content:
Hey Smallfolk!

We've been so humbled by the response to our first official gameplay trailer, and it's been wonderful to welcome many new people to the Smalland community who discovered us through E3.

For new members, we have an [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/768200/discussions/0/4679778856505610114/]FAQ[/url] of some common questions that may help you get acquainted.

Here are some great community questions and answers!

[u][b]Will the player character be voiced acted or silent?[/b][/u]

Currently silent. We’ve decided on this course because of a couple of things; Budget is one of them, and the other is flexibility as with v/o you need to have everything locked down and ready very early. Now, this could definitely be an option during Early Access, so we’ll see what happens as there are NPCs and they are important to the game as they help explain the lore as well as your goals. They all have very distinct personalities and backstory too, which will be revealed as you ally yourself with a faction over time and trust.

[u][b]Will there be an arachnophobia mode?[/b][/u]

This has definitely come up previously on the Smalland Discord Channel. Since Smalland is jam-packed with creepy crawly creatures, it's kind of pointless to have an arachnophobia mode when there are so many other potentially scary things in the game. You would have to turn off a lot of content and it would be a very different experience. So while it's great in theory, we have decided against it since it’s such a Creature focused game.

[u][b]Maybe I'm wrong, but I remember an old Smalland trailer with a train...What happened to it?[/b][/u]

You're not wrong, there was a train in the original trailer. This is not something that's been ignored, and we have a train ready to be implemented, the thing that's stopping it is why is there a train on a branch in the middle of a forest?

We’ve spent a lot of time trying to justify this, and it doesn't make sense. We’ve worked very hard to create a sense of fantasy but also plausible belief, and getting a working train on a branch doesn't make sense. What is powering it? What is its purpose? 

Every idea we have is better when we use a creature instead, it's more fun and suits the game so much better. Also riding on a toy train is kind of just like riding on a train since you’re small. So elements, where you take advantage of the environment because of the height and perspective, work really well. Such as sneaking through gaps feels far better than it should, seeing something we as humans class as normal but experiencing it as Smallfolk is fun and memorable. But a tiny train to a tiny person is just a train.

So the train is there, rebuilt so it’s ready to work properly in-game and not a cutscene. But how to effectively use it so it makes sense or in a way that’s more fun than riding a Lizard, Hornet, or Grasshopper…. Feel free to jump into [url=https://discord.gg/smalland]Discord[/url] and make some suggestions.

notes.title: FAQ Friday #4
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

We're back with another FAQ Friday to give a bit of a deeper dive into some of the excellent questions raised by the community.

Let's get into it!

[u][b]Could we get an idea of how big the map is? Maybe compared to other survival games?[/b][/u]

It's big, it's huge, compared to other games is kind of hard as some games have detailed areas with lots to do and others are much bigger by comparison but have lots of less detailed areas to travel across. So a straight comparison isn't fair, but we could make a massive desert which would be hugely optimal but it wouldn't be fun, or a very small but detailed complex area that's great for gameplay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/957195b0f837e25b5e0ec51c8f9f837ced973bc8.jpg[/img]
 
However, we can confidently say it is very big, not just from your special perspective, but because exploration is a big focus, the map and areas to explore and discover has been a focus, and the feedback on how big the map is during our behind the scenes tests have come back really positive.

[u][b]Will there be some easter eggs regarding media, old and new, regarding the game subject matter to find and linked to achievements? IE: 1: Honey I Shrunk The Kids. 2: Fantastic Voyage 3: Any B-rated cheezy black and white "Sci-Fi" with giant bugs.[/b][/u]

Yeah hopefully, we looked at a lot of B-Movies as references such as Honey I Shrunk the Kids, Them, The Incredible Shrinking Man, and how they emphasise and build up certain elements. Easter Eggs and things to find that are just fun is something we think is important. Kev is a massive fan of B-Movies and Cult Movies, so it's been fun "educating" the rest of the team!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/f13202930771ac95c7aea4c7b49c0e9de449f023.gif[/img]

[u][b]When you're playing multiplayer can you see the other players from a far distance, like their name above them?[/b][/u]

Yes, but we go one step further. One of the unique things about Smalland, especially if you're in first person, is because everything is giant your brain is used to seeing things a certain way so it's sometimes harder to appreciate the depth of what you're looking at. So an object looks like it's 10 meters away, but really it's a 500 meters (as a very rough example).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/82bff76b2c1cbb53f2781ed34f06db7fe3dd0542.jpg[/img]

 Seeing players in the distance as tiny specs is important as you can help one another, and it gives you the reality of just how far away everything is and makes you feel tiny, so we need to push this more, and names above heads are great up close but not that kind of distance.
 
So, the characters of Smalland have evolved with Bat-like ears and insect-like antenna which have helped them survive. These antennae give off a glow at a distance so they make players and NPCs alike identifiable from very far away.

This is also one of the reasons they have been mistaken as faerie folk, as they look like Will-o'-the-Wisps from a distance. A Will-o'-the-Wisp is a name for a ghostly light that legend has it is seen in fields and forests and often lures travellers off their path, or, helpfully getting them back on their path. There are legends of these sprites, orbs, or ghostly flames in Asia, South America, the Netherlands, Wales, England, Scotland, and Ireland (and probably more).... so there has to be some truth to that, right?

Thanks again for some great questions and as always we're always on the lookout for some more to deep dive into!

notes.content:
Hey everyone!

We get lots of great questions from the community so we’re aiming to pull out a couple of questions every couple of weeks to answer in a bit more depth.

We would love to invite you to join the Smalland discord to really get involved in the conversation which you can find [url=https://discord.gg/smalland]here[/url].

Off the back of the reveal of our lovely new artwork and screenshots, a couple of good questions came up that we thought would be great to address for our first FAQ Friday post!

[u][b]Can we build on the side of trees?[/b][/u]

We're currently working on a system where you can build anything you like, anywhere, but also have specific areas where you can build your intricate bases around a certain point, and then be able to move servers, play with old friends, new friends, by yourself, whatever, and take your base with you. This adds both creative freedoms but also lots of technical constraints and server details that we're looking into, but that's our goal.

The construction itself is a fairly standard approach to survival games, but weather and seasons also play into it. It's also going to be stylised around the lore of Smalland as there are certain characteristics that we want to reflect.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/2257644cab34be4168369df535b79f42b547f7e4.gif[/img]

[u][b]Can I ride on dragonflies?[/b][/u]

Yes, you can ride on Dragonflies! They are found in areas of Smalland with still water and while they are more scarce, they do survive Autumn and Winter. 

Because of how common they are, and that they are able to survive all seasons, the Dragonfly acts as a reliable noble steed and companion. 

It has a method of attack but will rely on the player doing most of the work in combat. The Dragonfly is built for speed, so whilst it won’t have the highest health or armour, it’s fast and has the massive advantage of flight.

notes.title: A fresh new look!
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

We’ve got something a bit different for you today! We are very excited to share with you a refresh of Smalland’s Key Art, an updated and more accurate description of the game, and all new in-game screenshots on the Steam page. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31398346/b654e3927fc638f4ad8af72c676f3b5cb4ffc245.jpg[/img]

The game has come such a long way in just under a year since Merge Games restarted development, and this update aligns everything with the current state of the game, and the vision of the final product.

Our goal has always been to evolve the original concept and the elements that looked fun and enticing and to make them into a fully working and playable reality.

Community is absolutely at the core of Smalland. Everything we do is measured against feedback, interest, and expectations from the community, focusing on the core aspect that this is an imaginative perspective that we want players to see themselves in.

As a survival game it is important that the feeling of struggle, and the subsequent satisfaction of accomplishment, are felt throughout. Along with the sense of unknown that Survival games need, plus the feeling of ownership that comes with not just building a base or a home, but with exploration and the familiarity of friends and foes you get to know in the game world.

Because of this, we have added narrative and lore to help guide players and create goals not just within the game’s fiction, ultimately becoming a saviour, but goals for the sandbox elements too such as Mounts and Pets. Factions that have their own ideals that you may or may not agree with, creatures that can be allies or enemies. It’s entirely up to you how you approach this, just like any other element of a good survival game. Discovery is part of the fun.

So, it's important that you the player are immersed in Smalland, the new additions will help guarantee this whilst also staying true to the original concept; a massive adventure on a tiny scale, with a perspective that’s exciting and on some level relatable, playing alongside friends as you explore the strange open world.

Whether you have been following Smalland from the very beginning, joined us recently or found your way here some time in-between, we would like to take this opportunity to say a massive thank you to our fans for the support. 

We genuinely appreciate the community that has arisen around Smalland so much. The team always listens to your feedback and it helps so much. We’re excited to share this important stage in the development of Smalland with you and properly share the full vision of the game.

Keep looking out for updates, please check out the new Steam Page and it would be great if you added us to your Wishlist. We’ll also be aiming for more Twitter updates and of course the team are always hanging around in our Discord Channel. 

We’ve seen some amazing fan art already, so with this updated look at the visuals of Smalland we would definitely encourage you to share your fan art with us, we love to see it!

From the Smalland Team and Merge Games, thanks for your time and support.
Stay safe, and we’ll see you soon.

notes.title: A quick update
notes.content:
Hello everyone! We're sorry for the lack of updates lately. But we've got some news for you now.

When we started development of Smalland, we had one developer doing the entire game in something called 'blueprint programming' in Unreal Engine. The problem with this type of programming is that it's incompatible with most PC and multiplayer programs out there. On January 25th, we announced that we were bringing in a few developers. We quickly decided it'd be a good idea to start the game from scratch, this time using C++ programming. C++ is ten times faster than blueprint, and will allow us to deliver the survival experience you all deserve! With this new programming language, the performance will be more efficient, the multiplayer servers will now have over sixty player slots, and additionally, this means that you'll be able to look forward to new exciting features and updates in the coming months.

For the past three months, we've been working on the skeleton of our game. Most of it is non-visual stuff, but we're also working on things like animations, models, and level design! As a sneak peek, here's a look at our working UI model:

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31398346/d4078e7b7505ed933d8d4412807d9d7798b98b83.png[/img]

We'll have some more exciting stuff for everyone to see next month. We're all working really hard to make SMALLAND a reality, and we appreciate your patience and support. Thank you!
